value.produces: boot.qcow2 (1992 kernel floppy, ROOT_DEV retargeted to /dev/hd1) + hda.qcow2 (minix root filesystem + swap partition) + hdb.qcow2 (blank slave, required by hd.c)

value.kbd_note: Linux 0.12 text console at a root '[/usr/root]#' shell: every typed char echoes immediately. Non-destructive probe: `cat /etc/passwd`. The fixture is a logged-in root shell (root has no password in this root filesystem), so no login is needed.
value.note: PC speaker only; Linux 0.12 has no mouse driver of any kind -> mouse N/A

labctl.notes: no exec channel: use 'labctl sh' (blind, QMP keyboard) — Linux 0.12 predates every Linux networking stack (the first was 0.96b, mid-1992), so there is no in-guest network to reach

render.stationsManifestPrelude: # linux012 (VMID 205) — Linux 0.12, January 1992: boots its original kernel floppy, roots from IDE.

launcherParity.reason: registry source pins pc-i440fx-11.0,acpi=off with backend-only PC-speaker routing; no -cpu is passed (QEMU's i386/KVM default is what the golden was baked against), and both IDE disks carry the explicit CHS 64/16/32 that Linux 0.12's hd.c divides against

museum.arch: i386 — 80386 protected mode only, deliberately: 0.12 will not run on a 286
museum.notes: Live streamhost station, text console only — no pointer, no network, because Linux 0.12 has neither. The guest boots the original 1992 kernel floppy (bootimage-0.12-20040306) and mounts the original 1.4 MB minix root filesystem, moved onto an IDE partition because QEMU 11 cannot drive 0.12's floppy.c through a root-floppy read — which is Linus's own documented install path (RELNOTES-0.12 steps 4-7), not a modern shortcut. Partition 2 is a real swap area, so the kernel prints `Swap device ok: 1023 pages (4190208 bytes) swap-space` on every boot and 0.12's headline feature is genuinely running. Root has no password. The whole userland is 6 free blocks short of full, exactly as a 1.44 MB root floppy was.
eraSoftware: GNU file utilities (ls, cp, mv, rm, chmod)
GNU text utilities (cat, head, tail, grep, sed, uniq, paste)
museum.periodBrowser: none — Linux had no networking stack of any kind until 0.96b in mid-1992
museum.blurb: Four months after Linus Torvalds posted that he was writing "just a hobby, won't be big and professional like gnu", this is what it had become: a kernel small enough to boot off one floppy, with a root filesystem that fits on another. Version 0.12 is the one that mattered. It added demand paging — the first Linux that could swap to disk, and so the first that ran comfortably on the 2 MB machines most people actually owned. And its release notes quietly changed the licence to the GNU copyleft, the decision that made everything after it possible. It was also the version on the screen in January 1992 while Andrew Tanenbaum was explaining on Usenet why it was obsolete.

reset.fixture: Minix 2.0.4 logged in as root (no password) at the '#' shell, screen showing `uname -a` (Minix minix 2 0.4 i686) and `ls /usr/src` (LICENSE boot etc inet lib tmp / Makefile commands fs kernel mm tools). Text console, no pointer surface. Golden baked 2026-09-13 on /data/vms/sandbox/minix2/smoke/rig.sh, restore-proven with `loadvm golden` (a typed echo line vanished and the fixture returned); keyboard proven at the fleet floor 40/40 by typing `echo KEYBOARD PROOF minix2 2026-09-13` and reading the echo back off the framebuffer.

notes: root filesystem moved from the 1992 root floppy onto an IDE partition; see docs/lab/LINUX012-WAVE.md for the seven configurations that proved the floppy path unusable under QEMU 11
hdb.qcow2 is blank on purpose and must not be removed: hd.c polls the status port before selecting a drive, and panics with no slave attached
